name: Spoilage System
description: Per-item freshness that ticks down inside the inventory and converts food into waste. Freshness is item metadata with a half-life per item class; spoiled items are CONVERTED, not deleted — into a spoiled variant or compost — because silent deletion punishes players for not reading a wiki, while conversion keeps the loss legible and even useful. The tick batches on day boundaries and timer completions rather than per-frame, because spoilage is a logistics pressure, not a twitch mechanic, and per-frame freshness is a float nobody can read. Preservation (salt, icebox, drying rack) is a drain multiplier supplied by the container holding the item, so storage gameplay composes without this component knowing what an icebox is.

inputs.name: defaultHalfLifeDays
inputs.description: Game days for an unclassed perishable to lose half its freshness. Item classes override this in data; the default exists so a designer who forgets gets a gentle clock, not immortal food.

inputs.name: tickMode
inputs.description: 'daily' batches decay on world.dawnStarted; 'timer' ticks on utility.timerCompleted for finer-grained modes. Daily is the default because one visible freshness step per morning is readable; hourly wobble is not.

inputs.name: spoiledItemSuffix
inputs.description: Suffix mapping a spoiled item id to its converted form ('berries' to 'berries_spoiled'). Conversion target is a naming convention, not a lookup table, so new perishables spoil correctly the day they are authored.

inputs.name: containerPreserveMultiplier
inputs.description: Drain multiplier applied when the containing storage declares preservation. Read from the container per tick; this component never asks what KIND of storage it is, which is why iceboxes and salt pits both work without code here.

outputs.name: spoiledTotalCount
outputs.description: Lifetime count of items converted to spoiled form. A telemetry number for tuning the half-life ladder — if nothing ever spoils, the clock is decorative.
